name: National priorities
note: The generic focus tree for every country without its own, in the style of the Russian model tree: focuses build, grant and swap national spirits (data/spirits/generic.json), unlock the project decisions, cost money and grant research. The political branch has a steady course (the historical path) and six mutually exclusive alternatives; each brings to power only a real party of the country's data and shows only where one exists, except the military junta. It names no real place, so claims and war goals on the nationalist paths target the least friendly neighbour. Alternatives are a counterfactual, not a claim about the parties. Effects are gameplay estimates.

focuses.name: The question of power
focuses.description: Decide whether the political order stays as it is or changes course.

focuses.name: A steady course
focuses.description: Keep the political order as it is. This is the path most countries took.

focuses.name: Institutional continuity
focuses.description: Keep the civil service and the courts out of party politics.

focuses.name: Liberal opening
focuses.description: Open the political system to real competition; the liberal parties gain ground.

focuses.name: A free press
focuses.description: End state pressure on the media.

focuses.name: A liberal government
focuses.description: The most popular liberal party forms the government and calls free elections.

focuses.name: Rule of law
focuses.description: Independent courts, full civil liberties and an anti-corruption drive.

focuses.name: Socialist turn
focuses.description: Hard times turn voters toward the socialist and communist parties.

focuses.name: Workers' movement
focuses.description: Strikes and committees in the factories rally behind the party.

focuses.name: A socialist government
focuses.description: The most popular socialist party takes power and rules as the single governing party.

focuses.name: Public ownership
focuses.description: Bring the large industries and the banks into public ownership and plan investment.

focuses.name: Nationalist turn
focuses.description: Nationalist parties gain from a mood of national grievance.

focuses.name: Patriotic rallies
focuses.description: Mass rallies around national symbols and grievances.

focuses.name: A nationalist government
focuses.description: The most popular nationalist party forms the government.

focuses.name: National sovereignty first
focuses.description: Restrict immigration, limit foreign influence and raise new divisions.

focuses.name: Claims on the border
focuses.description: Claim border provinces of the least friendly neighbour.

focuses.name: Ultranationalist turn
focuses.description: In a deep crisis, an ultranationalist party gains a mass following and seeks an authoritarian state. This is a counterfactual, not a claim about the party's aims.

focuses.name: A street movement
focuses.description: Marches and rallies spread the movement in the cities.

focuses.name: Seizure of power
focuses.description: The ultranationalist party takes power, abolishes elections and rules as the only party.

focuses.name: National mobilisation
focuses.description: State control of the press, universal military training and a war economy.

focuses.name: The lost territories
focuses.description: Claim the border lands of the least friendly neighbour and prepare for war.

focuses.name: Religious turn
focuses.description: Religious parties gain support as faith becomes central to politics.

focuses.name: Faith networks
focuses.description: Charities and congregations organise for the religious parties.

focuses.name: A religious government
focuses.description: The most popular religious party forms the government.

focuses.name: Faith in public life
focuses.description: An official religion and religious education in state schools.

focuses.name: The army steps in
focuses.description: With the state in crisis, the generals prepare to take over.

focuses.name: Military council
focuses.description: The armed forces remove the government. The coup may fail.

focuses.name: Martial order
focuses.description: A state of emergency, a curfew and military courts.

focuses.name: Officers in the economy
focuses.description: Army-run companies and a larger defence industry.

focuses.name: Return to the barracks
focuses.description: The council hands power to an elected government.

focuses.name: National agenda
focuses.description: Set out the government's priorities for its term.

focuses.name: Strengthen institutions
focuses.description: Invest in the civil service and the courts.

focuses.name: Public outreach
focuses.description: Explain the government's programme across the country.

focuses.name: Anti-corruption drive
focuses.description: Audit public contracts and strengthen oversight bodies. Unlocks anti-corruption audits.

focuses.name: Civic education
focuses.description: Fund civic education in schools and universities.

focuses.name: Civil service reform
focuses.description: Hire and promote officials on merit.

focuses.name: E-government
focuses.description: Taxes, permits and records online.

focuses.name: Regional development
focuses.description: Roads, schools and clinics for the poorer regions.

focuses.name: National reconciliation
focuses.description: Bring regions and communities into the political settlement.

focuses.name: Economic council
focuses.description: Convene ministers, employers and unions on the economy.

focuses.name: Fiscal review
focuses.description: Review spending and the tax base.

focuses.name: Infrastructure programme
focuses.description: Build and repair roads, rail and ports. Unlocks public works.

focuses.name: Austerity
focuses.description: Cut spending to balance the budget.

focuses.name: Stimulus
focuses.description: Borrow to fund public investment.

focuses.name: A balanced budget
focuses.description: The deficit is closed and borrowing becomes cheaper.

focuses.name: Market reform
focuses.description: Open sectors to competition and private investment.

focuses.name: State-led development
focuses.description: Direct investment through state enterprises and development banks.

focuses.name: Industrial parks
focuses.description: Serviced land and tax breaks for new factories.

focuses.name: Ports and airports
focuses.description: Modern ports and airports for trade.

focuses.name: Export drive
focuses.description: Manufacturing for export markets.

focuses.name: Energy security
focuses.description: Diversify energy supplies and build new power plants.

focuses.name: Fuel refining
focuses.description: Refine fuel at home instead of importing it.

focuses.name: Modern agriculture
focuses.description: Credit, irrigation and machinery for farmers.

focuses.name: Innovation agenda
focuses.description: Fund research and new industries.

focuses.name: Sovereign wealth fund
focuses.description: Save resource revenue for future generations.

focuses.name: Long-term growth plan
focuses.description: Commit to a ten-year plan for growth.

focuses.name: Defence review
focuses.description: Review threats, forces and budgets.

focuses.name: Professional forces
focuses.description: Move to an all-volunteer professional military.

focuses.name: Mass reserve
focuses.description: Keep universal service and a large trained reserve. Unlocks mobilisation of the reserves.

focuses.name: Intelligence reform
focuses.description: Reorganise and fund the intelligence services.

focuses.name: Force modernisation
focuses.description: Replace ageing equipment.

focuses.name: Defence industry
focuses.description: Build arms and ammunition at home. Unlocks arms orders.

focuses.name: Border security
focuses.description: Tighten control of borders and ports.

focuses.name: Air force
focuses.description: New aircraft and air bases.

focuses.name: Armoured units
focuses.description: Tanks and armoured vehicles.

focuses.name: Coastal navy
focuses.description: Patrol boats and a naval base.

focuses.name: Special forces
focuses.description: A special operations command.

focuses.name: A new doctrine
focuses.description: Rewrite the doctrine for modern war.

focuses.name: Armed neutrality
focuses.description: Strong defences and no alliances.

focuses.name: Peacekeepers
focuses.description: Send units on UN peacekeeping missions for experience and standing.

focuses.name: Foreign policy review
focuses.description: Define the country's place in the world.

focuses.name: Regional cooperation
focuses.description: Seek closer ties and trade with neighbours.

focuses.name: Independent course
focuses.description: Keep freedom of action and limit foreign influence.

focuses.name: Trade agreements
focuses.description: Free-trade agreements with the main partners.

focuses.name: International standing
focuses.description: Raise the country's profile in international bodies.

focuses.name: Arms purchases abroad
focuses.description: Buy modern equipment from foreign suppliers.

focuses.name: Development aid
focuses.description: Attract loans and grants for development.

focuses.name: The diaspora
focuses.description: Courting citizens abroad for investment and remittances.

focuses.name: Regional leadership
focuses.description: Lead the region's diplomacy and mediate its disputes.

focuses.name: Social policy
focuses.description: Set the government's priorities for health, schools and science.

focuses.name: Public health
focuses.description: Clinics, vaccination and clean water.

focuses.name: Schools for all
focuses.description: More schools and teachers.

focuses.name: Universal healthcare
focuses.description: Public health insurance for everyone.

focuses.name: Research universities
focuses.description: Fund universities and laboratories. Unlocks research grants.

focuses.name: Housing programme
focuses.description: Affordable housing in the growing cities.

focuses.name: Keep the talent
focuses.description: Better pay for researchers and doctors so they stay.

focuses.name: Digital society
focuses.description: Broadband and digital skills across the country.
